answer: One defense is a seasoning bond: each new agent locks a stake that only unlocks after months of verified useful work, and every completed job adds an audit thread to its public record. An attacker trying to forge a hundred fake identities must fund a hundred bonds and wait out a hundred seasoning periods, while the required bond rises in a spiral whenever identity creation spikes. A fresh account with no history carries an umber mark of unproven trust and gets only low-value tasks until it earns its way up. Forging reputation is far slower and costlier than buying it.
